title: Draft Galley
heading: Your document — draft 1, for review
subtitle: The document in full with review flags spliced in where they apply. Each flag carries its severity, how it was grounded, its evidence and a proposed edit. Decide with the buttons; decisions are saved as you go.
governance: Consequence model. Accepted flags are applied in the next commit and named in its message; rejected and deferred flags stay on record with the note. For a published record, replace this with: accepted flags produce a versioned update with a changelog entry — the record readers have cited is never edited in place.
verified: State here what you checked and found clean — the numbers that agreed, the citations that were accurate, the figures that matched their data.
A reader needs to know what was verified, not only what was flagged.
method: Method. Markdown rendered with per-paragraph source-line markers; flags anchored by phrase and spliced after the paragraph they concern. Grounding: ran (executed and observed), read (opened the source), fetched (retrieved the cited work), assumed (not checked — recorded as such).
